title: Stability Sprint Garden — Seed Plan & Ops Playbook
body:
Purpose and overview:

This is a compact, experiment-first project plan for the "Stability Sprint Garden": a set of three short, cross-functional reliability experiments designed to seed, test, and then scale SLO patterns for model-serving routes that are high-cost / high-impact. The focus is intentionally pragmatic — run quick signal-led pilots, capture telemetry, and produce concrete guardrails + an ops playbook that product and platform teams can adopt.

Why a "garden" metaphor?
- Seed: small cost/latency experiments to validate signal collection and rollback behaviors.
- Sprout: run targeted pilots for a handful of services and verify tooling (dashboards, alerts, runbooks).
- Harvest: scale policies and automated fallbacks where pilots succeed.

Scope and constraints:
- Services: hosted inference routes (text-generation), embedders for user-facing search, 2 internal platform endpoints (health-check & routing).
- Timebox: 10 week program split into 3 waves (2w seed, 4w sprout, 4w harvest).
- Budget: reserve one SRE rotation + fractional platform and product support. Keep experiments non-invasive (no hard SLA changes).
- Success criteria: detectability and actionable alerts for 3 major failure modes, measurable improvement in error clarity, a reproducible SLO template + rollout checklist.

High-level timeline (weeks):
- Week 1–2 (Seed): instrumentation gaps, initial telemetry panels, quick hypothesis tests (prefix cache behavior, tail latency spikes under load).
- Week 3–6 (Sprout): pick 3 routes, enable SLOs (availability + latency), run canary traffic experiments, iterate runbooks and alert routing.
- Week 7–10 (Harvest): evaluate, codify playbook, recommend rollout to Dedicated & Private lanes.

Roles & owners (primary):
- Program lead: Ava Martinez (eng-sre) — program coordination + weekly syncs
- Observability lead: Marcus Li (observability) — dashboards, alert tuning, instrumentation PRs
- Platform lead: Ravi Singh (platform-engineering) — rollout mechanics, autoscaling policy test harness
- Product owner: Elena Petrov (product-hosted-api) — route selection, success metrics alignment with product metrics
- Solutions/CS liaison: Priya Shah — customer impact mapping, external comms draft
- SRE rotation: Jonah Rivera — on-call and incident shepherd for pilot windows

Deliverables:
- Telemetry checklist & gap report (seed end)
- SLO templates (availability + p50/p95 latency buckets) for generation and embedding routes
- Canary experiment recipes + traffic shaping scripts
- Per-route runbooks (playbook section + escalation matrix)
- Post-pilot evaluation deck with recommended rollouts and rollback criteria

Signal & metrics (what we will track):
- Core SLOs: request success rate (200-series vs 5xx/4xx), p50/p95/p99 latency on user-facing tokens, tail-in-fan (percent of requests that hit >Xms), model quality signal (basic posterior or logprob regression where available)
body_addendum:
(continued)

Operational signals to capture: prefix cache hit rate, KV-cache write contention, GPU queue length, batching efficiency, memory OOM events, request size distribution, cost-per-1000-tokens.

Experiment designs (short):
- Seed test A: Synthetic tails — controlled load to reproduce p99 spikes; verify alert sensitivity and suppression windows. Owner: Marcus.
- Seed test B: Prefix cache warm/cold — rapid scenario where cache miss rate shifts; validate graceful fallback path to smaller model variant. Owner: Ravi.
- Sprout pilot 1: Gen-route A — enable availability SLO 99.5% and latency SLO p95 < 350ms; run 2-week canary at 10% traffic. Owner: Elena + Ava.
- Sprout pilot 2: Embed-route B — emphasis on cost and latency; test batching settings and quantization suggestions from Optimize toolkit. Owner: Marcus + Platform.

Decision gates (per wave):
- Seed -> Sprout: telemetry completeness (>= 90% of planned metrics instrumented) AND at least one reproducible failure prototype with an actionable alert.
- Sprout -> Harvest: pilot meets availability and latency SLOs OR there is a clear mitigation pattern that reduces customer impact by >= 30% while keeping cost within threshold.

Runbook excerpt (playbook checklist):
1) Identify route & owners
2) Baseline metric capture (72h)
3) Create SLO in observability and annotate key vectors (model, quantization, batch config)
4) Configure alert routing (pager vs slack) and set suppression for canary windows
5) Run traffic experiment (load pattern + increment schedule)
6) Post-incident review template if SLO breach occurs

Communications and meetings:
- Weekly sync (Ava) — 30m, status + blockers. Invite list: owners + rotation SREs.
- Weekly demo (end of sprout) — 45m, show dashboards & playback of incidents.
- Incident bridge plan: use shared #sre-garden channel for initial triage, escalate to #sre-oncall if required.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: instrumentation false-positives. Mitigation: synthetic tests before enabling production alerts; use multi-signal (latency + error) for firing.
- Risk: customer-facing regressions during pilots. Mitigation: start at 5–10% traffic, automatic rollback hook if error rate > threshold for 5m.
- Risk: cross-team capacity constraints. Mitigation: prebook SRE rotation, limit scope per wave.

Dependencies:
- Observability PRs: dashboards + alert rules (ENGINF-1324)
- Platform: test cluster for canary traffic and temporary model-variant push (SRE-847)
- Product: route signoff and user-impact mapping (Confluence doc link in linked_artifacts)

Open questions / notes to self (quick):
- Do we need a separate SLO for downstream model quality (semantic drift)? (ask Research/Applied ML)
- Which routes have existing customer SLAs that block canary traffic? (check CS atlas)
- How to capture cost delta precisely for quantization pilot (per-call cost attribution needed)

Immediate next steps (week 0):
- Align owners and confirm rotation weeks (Ava) — due 2026-11-20
- Observability quick audit: Marcus to produce telemetry gap report — due 2026-11-22
- Platform to provision canary namespace and traffic shaping scripts — Ravi due 2026-11-24
- Product to nominate two candidate routes with expected user impact and traffic patterns — Elena due 2026-11-24

Checklist before enabling alerts in production:
- Dashboard coverage for p50/p95/p99 + errors (yes/no)
- Synthetic test reproducer (yes/no)
- Rollback automation validated (yes/no)
- Communication channels pre-configured (yes/no)

Appendix: short glossary
- SLO: Service Level Objective
- Canary: small percentage of production traffic for testing
- Prefix cache: model-serving optimization to avoid repeated token decoding work
- Fallthrough model: smaller/cheaper model variant used when main model fails or latency spikes

If you want to iterate on this doc, append notes below and tag me (@ava) in the SRE Slack thread.

-- Ava
